items.title: YouTube is testing auto-expanding video previews on TVs

 We’ve confirmed the behavior on Google TV, while users on Xbox, PS5, and Fire TV Stick have reported similar experiences. 
 The change isn’t widely available yet, suggesting it could be a limited test, although YouTube hasn’t officially confirmed anything. 

YouTube appears to be changing how video previews work on its Google TV app, with previews now expanding into full-screen playback roughly 40 seconds in. We’ve independently observed the change on Google TV , though similar user reports on Reddit confirm that the change isn’t limited to Google’s own platform.

This appears to be a relatively new development. Although I spotted the change over the weekend, user reports on Reddit suggest the behavior has been around since early November at the very least.

items.title: Pixel owners are seeing a weird animation bug when closing recent apps
items.summary:
Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Some Pixel owners are experiencing a glitch with the recent apps screen. 
 Visual ghosting occurs when swiping up to close an app. 
 Users say that the visual bug started happening after the October update. 

Android has some pretty smooth animations, from the shrinking transition you see when exiting an app to the subtle bounce when opening Quick Settings . The animations are so smooth that some people may not even notice them. That’s why when the fluidity of these animations breaks, it stands out like a sore thumb. Unfortunately, it appears a bug is doing just that when closing out of apps.

Some Pixel owners are experiencing a visual glitch when trying to close an app via the recent apps screen. To close an app on the recent apps screen, you can either swipe up on the app or scroll all the way to the left and hit the Clear all button. According to reports , swiping up on an app causes a trail (visual ghosting) to appear instead of the smooth animation that should happen.
items.t: Pixel owners are seeing a weird animation bug when closing recent apps

items.title: Gemini is getting text message and email control through Channels
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is introducing Gemini Channels to remotely interact with the AI service. 
 Users can set up Channels over both text messaging and email. 
 Text support requires RCS, and may be limited by your carrier. 

Google already gives us a million and one different way to access Gemini through apps , web interfaces, and more, and now it looks like we’re getting a new option for remotely interacting with Gemini, as Google introduces Channels for text messages.

We first noticed noted Google preparing to add this new Channels option in Gemini settings, but it wasn’t immediately clear what it was for. It led us to gemini.google.com/channels , which at the time just redirected to the main Gemini page. But today it looks like Google has finally flipped the switch on this live, and we can now see it for what it is: a way to interact with Gemini over text or email (Thanks: Joshua).
items.t: Gemini is getting text message and email control through Channels

items.title: Your paid Galaxy AI subscription could unlock extra custom cards in Now Brief
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung may let users buy a Galaxy AI subscription to add more than three custom cards in Now Brief. 
 Additionally, the custom card limits page in One UI 9.5 shows that users can buy AI Plan credits if they need more than the daily allowance. 
 While each device may have separate custom card limits, AI plan credits could be shared across devices paired with the Samsung account. 

All signs point to Samsung charging consumers for additional Galaxy AI features, and a new leak may have revealed how it could apply to custom cards in Now Brief . Samsung currently restricts custom cards to just three, but One UI 9.5 could let users pay for more.

Custom cards were introduced with One UI 9 to give users more control over the cards that appear in Now Brief, with the ability to display cards from Weather, Health, or Videos categories at specific intervals. SamMobile has spotted updated entries on the Custom card limits page, showing how users can “upgrade to a paid plan” to add more than the three cards available to Standard/free AI plan users.
items.t: Your paid Galaxy AI subscription could unlock extra custom cards in Now Brief

items.title: How to hide the new macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator
items.summary:

items.title: Google AI Mode gets temporary threads for searches you don’t want saved
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode, similar to temporary chats in the Gemini app. 
 Temporary threads don’t appear in your history, draw on past preferences, or influence future personalization. 
 The feature is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile browsers in all languages supported by AI Mode. 

Google has spent much of 2026 improving AI Mode’s ability to get to know you. Earlier this year, the company brought Personal Intelligence to AI Mode , allowing Search to draw on your Gmail and Google Photos data for more personalized answers. More recently, we even uncovered evidence that Google is working on letting you pin AI Mode conversations for easy access. As useful as these features are, there are times when you’d rather keep certain searches out of your history, and that’s where Google’s new temporary threads come in.

Starting today, Google is rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode, letting you ask questions without those conversations appearing in your search history or influencing future recommendations. This could come in handy when researching a surprise gift, exploring a topic out of curiosity, or looking up something personal that you don’t want Google bringing up again.
items.t: Google AI Mode gets temporary threads for searches you don’t want saved

items.title: Oura Ring’s new Jet Lag feature helps you adjust to different time zones
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Oura’s new Jet Lag feature uses your sleep history and chronotype to create personalized plans for adjusting to different time zones. 
 It recommends when to get sunlight, avoid bright light, sleep, and cut off caffeine, while tracking your recovery and offering post-trip insights. 
 The feature is rolling out globally for Oura Ring Gen 3 and newer users. 

Traveling to a new country is exciting, but jet lag? Not so much. You could land in the morning, ready to explore, only to find yourself struggling to stay awake a few hours later. And when it’s finally time to sleep, your body might have other plans. Oura wants to make those first few days a little easier with its new Jet Lag feature, which uses your sleep data to help your body adjust to a different time zone.

It looks at your sleep history and chronotype (your body’s natural sleep and wake preferences) to create a personalized plan. It also estimates when your body reaches its lowest temperature, typically around 4 AM, to better understand your internal sleep cycle.
items.t: Oura Ring’s new Jet Lag feature helps you adjust to different time zones

The Warby Parker collection is a different story, as all of its Alden, Wren, and Reid frames are still available to pre-order in the US, with estimated ship dates of December 9 or December 21, depending on the model.

items.summary:
Huawei recently confirmed that it will unveil its new sub-brand, Osta, on November 20. The company also revealed that one of the upcoming devices will be called the Osta O1 Pro. Now, a leaked live image has offered a first look at the phone's design.

The live image, circulating on Chinese social media platform Weibo, shows the alleged Osta O1 Pro next to Huawei's Pura X View.

items.title: Huawei Mate X8 RAM and storage options revealed as reservations open
items.summary:
Last week we told you that the Mate X8 was rumored to launch on November 24, and today Huawei made that official. The foldable will be unveiled at an event in China at 14:30 local time on that day, and it's already listed on the company's Vmall online store, where you can reserve one.

The listing reveals that the Mate X8 will come in four memory versions: 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB, 16GB/512GB, and 16GB/1TB, with the two 16GB variants being Collector's Editions. That's the same lineup of RAM and storage options that the Mate X7 was offered in last year.
